knowledgePattern: Find a polygonal area between two modulus graphs

hints.title: Sketch the two vertices
hints.body: Locate each modulus vertex and label the gradients of its two straight arms.
hints.recap: Use the sign of the inner expression to replace a modulus by the correct linear formula.
hints.pitfall: A modulus formula can change inside the enclosed interval.
hints.pause: Find the two intersections using the appropriate arms.

recall.reminder: Use the sign of the inner expression to replace a modulus by the correct linear formula.

hints.title: Measure the gap
hints.body: You can work with the vertical difference of the two graphs; on each straight section, its area is a triangle or trapezium.
hints.recap: A region can be split into simple geometric pieces or found by subtracting surrounding areas.
hints.pitfall: Use the height of the gap, not the height of only one graph.
hints.pause: Calculate the separate pieces and add them.

recall.reminder: A region can be split into simple geometric pieces or found by subtracting surrounding areas.

solution:
1. The lower V has vertex (1,0), and the upper inverted V has vertex (−2,6). For x<−2, their difference (upper minus lower) is 6+3x<0, so no enclosed portion is missed there.

2. For −2≤x≤1, the vertical gap is (4−x)−(2−2x)=x+2. For x≥1, it is (4−x)−(2x−2)=6−3x. Thus the intersections are at x=−2 and x=2.

3. The gap rises linearly from 0 to 3 on [−2,1], then falls to 0 on [1,2]. Its area is 12·3·3+12·1·3=6. Answer D.
